_doc: PRE-REGISTERED candidate list + evaluation contract for the EXPECTED-MOVE / VIX1D entry gate test (PROFIT-P5-EXPECTED-MOVE-PREREG). Frozen BEFORE any candidate is run (exploratory != confirmatory -- no re-picks after seeing results; FAIL is publishable). REGISTRATION ONLY: this file specifies the exact hypothesis, gate formula variants, population, window, battery, and kill bar. The run is dispatched separately once the OPRA option-bar cache is free. No test was executed to produce this file.
runner: NOT YET BUILT -- proposed path backtest/tools/expected_move_gate_study.py. This file is the exact contract that runner must satisfy: same population/window/battery/pass-bar as specified here, no substitutions without a new frozen version.
scheduling_note: Same OPRA option-bar cache dependency and queue position as prereg-morning-gate-2026-07-11.json (analysis/recommendations/) -- both P3 and P5 need backtest/data/options/ for option-premium math and are queued sequentially behind the crew currently using it (FDR-16 real-fills confirmation + P5-cohort top-cell confirm, per queue.md).

mechanism_source.core_claim: The at-the-money straddle price x ~0.85 gives the market's own 1-standard-deviation expected range for the session (standard practitioner formula, cited sources MenthorQ/Skavinski). When that range is too narrow to plausibly clear a trade's premium/spread cost, the day structurally can't pay and the signal should be skipped or downsized.
mechanism_source.evidence_quality_tag: [PRACTITIONER] formula, cross-checked against [EXCHANGE] primary data (CBOE VIX1D methodology, purpose-built for 0DTE, launched April 2023) and one [ACADEMIC] paper on VIX1D's documented overnight-bias/decay shape.
mechanism_source.portability: Path A (used here): compute directly from the SAME Alpaca option-chain data this project's own OPRA cache already holds -- zero new data source, zero new infra. Path B (VIX1D as a cross-check label) is NOT in scope for this pre-registration (would require a new external feed) -- noted as a possible future disclosure-only addition, never load-bearing for this study's pass/fail.

hypothesis: 0DTE ribbon_ride entries taken on session-days (or at intraday moments) where the market's own expected range is unusually compressed relative to what the trade needs to clear (premium cost + spread, or the distance to TP1) have structurally worse expectancy than entries taken when the expected range is ample -- because a trigger can fire correctly but the day simply lacks the realized movement to pay for it, independent of trigger quality.

hypothesis_provenance.generated_by: markdown/research/EXTERNAL-0DTE-MECHANISMS-2026-07-11.md mechanism #1 (external practitioner/exchange literature, NOT this repo's own 9-day sample -- disclosed distinction from the P3 morning-gate study, whose hypothesis DID come from the 9-day window).
hypothesis_provenance.corroborating_context: analysis/deep-research/2026-07-11-ledger-forensics.md section 4 notes VIX was pinned 15.19-20.64 for the entire 9-day live sample -- i.e. the live window cannot itself distinguish a genuine expected-move effect from noise (no regime variation to correlate against). This is the reason the full-history evaluation window below matters: the 9-day window structurally cannot test this hypothesis on its own.
hypothesis_provenance.exclusion_rationale: Matches the project's own no-peeking discipline (same exclusion as PROFIT-P3): this window is reserved as a future confirmatory check, not blended into the frozen evaluation below.

primary.rationale: Same scoping logic as PROFIT-P3 (C29: gate effects don't transfer across setups without independent verification) -- ribbon_ride is this project's highest-volume live setup and the one the deep-research synthesis is built around.

population_scope.explicit_note: unlike PROFIT-P3, this mechanism has no a priori conflict with the OTHER live setups' own time-of-day design (vwap_continuation etc. are about WHEN in the morning, not about the SESSION'S total expected range) -- so a future wider-scope run is plausible, but this registration freezes ribbon_ride ONLY to keep the first confirmatory test scoped and interpretable. Widening scope requires a NEW frozen version, not an amendment.

session_expected_move.atm_straddle_price_at_open: sum of the day's ATM (nearest-strike-to-spot) 0DTE call bar close + put bar close, sampled at the FIRST option bar at/after 09:35 ET (matches the existing v15.3 entry-gate floor -- no pre-floor data used, consistent with every other gate in this engine).
session_expected_move.data_source: backtest/data/options/*.csv (the SAME cached OPRA contract bars used by exit_shape_parity_study.py / structure_stop_study.py / t4_exit_matrix.py -- Path A, zero new data).

remaining_expected_move.rationale: standard sqrt-time scaling of expected range (consistent with Black-Scholes-style time-decay of variance) -- 375 = total RTH minutes 09:30-16:00. Disclosed as a modeling choice, not an empirically-fit parameter, per this repo's no-repick discipline.
remaining_expected_move.minutes_remaining_def: minutes from the signal's ET timestamp to 16:00 ET (session close), floored at 0.

V1_SESSION_FLOOR_TRAILING_PCTILE.label: day-level regime filter -- skip ALL entries on a day whose expected-move-as-%-of-spot is unusually compressed vs recent history
V1_SESSION_FLOOR_TRAILING_PCTILE.formula: expected_move_pct = expected_move_dollars / SPY_price_at_open. Trailing window = expected_move_pct on the prior 20 TRADING days (shift-1, strictly causal -- never includes today's own value, C6 no-look-ahead).
V1_SESSION_FLOOR_TRAILING_PCTILE.gate_rule: SKIP every entry that day if today's expected_move_pct < the 25th percentile of the trailing-20-day window.
V1_SESSION_FLOOR_TRAILING_PCTILE.granularity: day-level (evaluated once, at the first entry-eligible bar of the day; applies uniformly to every signal that day).
V1_SESSION_FLOOR_TRAILING_PCTILE.rationale: the closest match to the mechanism doc's own 'smallest testable step' (skip when the ratio sits below a trailing percentile). Cheapest variant: one number per day, no per-trade delta/moneyness modeling.

V2_REMAINING_MOVE_VS_TP1_DISTANCE.label: per-trade gate -- skip a signal if the day's remaining expected move, translated into an implied option-premium ceiling, can't plausibly clear this trade's TP1 distance
V2_REMAINING_MOVE_VS_TP1_DISTANCE.formula: implied_premium_ceiling = remaining_expected_move_dollars(t) x delta_proxy_for_tier. entry_premium_needed_for_tp1 = entry_premium x tp1_premium_pct (SS-B: 1.0, i.e. +100%; CONTROL/current: 1.5, i.e. +150% -- the runner must state which exit shape's tp1_premium_pct it used, since PROFIT-P1 may change this value before this study runs).

delta_proxy_table.source: matches this project's own per-tier strike-selection language (CLAUDE.md 'The strategy' section: OTM-3 at $1K / OTM-2 at $2-10K / OTM-1 at $10-25K / ITM-2 at $25K+), NOT a live per-trade Greek (Alpaca option snapshot Greeks were not verified available for this registration -- disclosed approximation, not a live feed).
delta_proxy_table.disclosure: a FIXED table, not fit to this study's own data -- if the runner finds live Greeks are in fact available cheaply from the Alpaca option snapshot already used elsewhere in this repo (mcp__alpaca__get_option_snapshot), it MAY substitute real per-trade delta and must disclose the substitution explicitly (does not require a new frozen version since it strictly improves precision on the SAME formula, not a new formula).

V2_REMAINING_MOVE_VS_TP1_DISTANCE.gate_rule: SKIP this entry if implied_premium_ceiling < entry_premium_needed_for_tp1.
V2_REMAINING_MOVE_VS_TP1_DISTANCE.granularity: per-trade (evaluated at each individual signal's timestamp).
V2_REMAINING_MOVE_VS_TP1_DISTANCE.rationale: the most literal match to the task's 'skip signals whose distance-to-target exceeds remaining expected move' framing -- most mechanistically complete, at the cost of the disclosed delta-proxy approximation.

V3_PREMIUM_BUDGET_RATIO.label: per-trade gate -- skip a signal if its premium cost is too large a share of the WHOLE day's expected-move budget
V3_PREMIUM_BUDGET_RATIO.formula: budget_ratio = entry_premium / expected_move_dollars (using the SESSION-level expected_move_dollars, not the time-decayed remaining figure -- deliberately simpler than V2, no sqrt-time scaling, no delta proxy).
V3_PREMIUM_BUDGET_RATIO.gate_rule: SKIP this entry if budget_ratio > 0.35 (candidate threshold: don't pay more than 35% of the day's total expected-move budget for one contract).
V3_PREMIUM_BUDGET_RATIO.granularity: per-trade, but uses only the session-open expected move (no intraday time-decay modeling).
V3_PREMIUM_BUDGET_RATIO.rationale: the most literal match to the task's 'premium cost can't clear the expected-range math' framing -- simplest variant, Path-A-only, easiest to reason about and audit; a useful robustness contrast to V2's more elaborate time-decay + delta model.

opra_option_cache_coverage_at_freeze.verified_by: directory listing of backtest/data/options/*.csv at freeze time -- 8,669 contract files, earliest SPY250102*, latest SPY260708*

is_oos_split.convention_source: same calendar-year OOS_BOUNDARY convention as PROFIT-P3 (backtest/autoresearch/family_grind.py etc.) -- reused for consistency.

evaluation_window.signal_population_source: the SAME full-history ribbon_ride signal-generation path as PROFIT-P3 (family_grind.py / the mass-grind funnel) -- population consistency between the two P3/P5 studies is itself a cheap cross-check the runner should perform (the two studies' gate-OFF baselines must match exactly if both ran on the same generator; a mismatch means one of them drifted).

1_expectancy.metric: per-trade dollar expectancy AND total pnl, gate-ON (candidate applied) vs gate-OFF (baseline, no expected-move gate) on the primary population/window.
1_expectancy.pass_condition: gate-ON per-trade expectancy > gate-OFF per-trade expectancy (STRICTLY greater), via lib.simulator_real.simulate_trade_real, same signal population for both arms.

2_oos.metric: condition 1 evaluated separately on IS (2025) and OOS (2026, post-exclusion).
2_oos.pass_condition: gate-ON beats gate-OFF in BOTH slices.

3_random_entry_null.purpose: isolates whether the BLOCKED (compressed-expected-move) cohort's poor performance is specific to ribbon_ride's signal quality on those days, or a generic 'nothing works when the day is dead' property any random entry would also show.
3_random_entry_null.method: autoresearch.null_baseline.random_entry_null over the SAME blocked-day/blocked-signal set (V1: the blocked DAYS' full RTH window; V2/V3: the blocked SIGNALS' own timestamps), matched n/side-mix/strike/stop to the removed cohort's realized values, 10 deterministic seeds.
3_random_entry_null.pass_condition: the blocked cohort's own realized per-trade expectancy is <= the random-entry null's per_trade_mean for the same days/signals.

4_opposite_null.purpose: negative control -- rules out 'skip an arbitrary similarly-sized subset and it looks like an improvement' rather than a genuine expected-move mechanism.
4_opposite_null.method: mirror-image gate: apply the SAME threshold logic to the HIGH end instead of the low end (V1: skip days ABOVE the 75th percentile instead of below the 25th; V2/V3: skip trades with the LARGEST implied_premium_ceiling / smallest budget_ratio instead of the opposite), sized to block a comparable trade-count to the real candidate.
4_opposite_null.pass_condition: the high-end mirror gate does NOT produce a comparable-or-larger expectancy improvement than the real (low-end) candidate. If it does, 'skip on the extreme value of this metric, either direction' is doing the work, not the expected-move mechanism specifically.

5_concentration.metric: drop-top-3 (t4_exit_matrix.py battery() convention) applied independently to KEPT and REMOVED cohorts.
5_concentration.pass_condition: gate-ON's drop-top-3 expectancy still beats gate-OFF's drop-top-3 expectancy.

6_bh_fdr.method: backtest/autoresearch/ribbon_rejection_wick_battery.py's bh_fdr() at FDR_ALPHA=0.10, applied across the 3 candidate_ids_in_multiplicity_correction.
6_bh_fdr.pass_condition: candidate's stage-1 effect survives BH-FDR correction at alpha=0.10 across the 3-way comparison.

kill_criteria.statement: ANY of the following kills the candidate outright, regardless of other stages (mirrors PROFIT-P3's kill ladder):
kill_criteria.k1: stage 1 (expectancy) fails on the full net window.
kill_criteria.k2: stage 2 (OOS) fails on either the IS or OOS slice alone.
kill_criteria.k3: stage 4 (opposite_null) shows the high-end mirror gate produces a comparable-or-larger improvement -- the effect is not specifically about LOW expected move.
kill_criteria.k4: stage 6 (BH-FDR) rejects the candidate at alpha=0.10 after multiplicity correction.
kill_criteria.k5_no_lift_over_vix_gate: queue.md's own stated kill for this item: 'no lift over existing VIX gates' -- if gate-ON's improvement over gate-OFF is not meaningfully larger than what the SAME population already gets from the existing VIX-level gates on BULLISH_RECLAIM/BEARISH_REJECTION (puts want VIX rising/>20, calls want VIX falling/<17.2, per playbook.md), the candidate is redundant with a gate already live, not a new lever. The runner must report the VIX-gate-only baseline alongside gate-OFF for this comparison.
kill_criteria.k6_anchor_violation: the candidate would have blocked any of J's 3 source-of-truth anchor winners (see anchor_context_check below) -- an automatic MISCALIBRATED flag, mirroring the exact instruction in EXTERNAL-0DTE-MECHANISMS-2026-07-11.md mechanism #1's own kill condition ('if the anchor winners cluster on LOW expected-move days... a blanket expected-move gate would be actively anti-edge -- same failure mode as the retired STAIRSTEP_CONTINUATION setup').

pass_bar.aggregation: AND of stages 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 AND k5/k6 clear -- no partial credit.
pass_bar.min_n_disclosure: kept AND removed cohort n must each be reported; n<20 on either side is INSUFFICIENT_N, reported as inconclusive, not passed or failed.

anchor_context_check.purpose: MANDATORY disclosure -- this is the exact check EXTERNAL-0DTE-MECHANISMS-2026-07-11.md mechanism #1 names as the make-or-break test for this mechanism specifically ('cross-checked against the 3 real-money anchor winners... the gate must not have blocked any anchor winner, or it's miscalibrated').

reporting_requirement.winners: for EACH candidate, compute expected_move_dollars / remaining_expected_move / budget_ratio (as applicable) for each winner's actual entry (time pulled from journal/YYYY-MM-DD.md, not assumed). If any candidate's gate_rule would have produced SKIP on a winner's actual entry, the candidate is MISCALIBRATED regardless of aggregate battery result -- report this BEFORE the aggregate result, not buried after it.
reporting_requirement.losers: same computation for the 4 losers, disclosure only (context on whether the mechanism would have caught real losses too, not itself pass/fail-determinative -- a gate is not required to catch every loser to be useful, but IS required to never block a winner).

no_repick_clause: Once this file is frozen, no formula, delta-proxy table, threshold, population scope, window, or battery definition may be edited in light of results. A FAIL (or an INSUFFICIENT_N on all 3 candidates, or a k6 anchor violation) is a publishable, informative outcome, not a reason to adjust the pre-registration and re-run.
